title: Home Services Technician
tagline: AC care, electrical safety, plumbing and handyman skills for Dubai homes, and how to quote and run jobs like a pro.

superpower.name: Fix-It Pro
superpower.description: Keeps homes running: lower repair bills, and more from maintenance jobs.

syllabus: Week 1: Safety first, tools and how Dubai homes are built
Week 2: Air conditioning: how it works and how to maintain it
Week 3: Plumbing and electrical basics (and when to call a licensed specialist)
Week 4: Quoting, customer service and running your own jobs

weeks.title: Safety, Tools and Dubai Homes
weeks.objective: Work safely, use the right tools and understand how villas and apartments are serviced.

slides.title: Safety Before Everything
slides.body: Most trade injuries are avoidable: falls from ladders, electric shocks, cuts and eye injuries. Professionals assess risk before every job, isolate power and water before working, and wear protection.
bullets: Isolate the circuit at the distribution board (DB) and test it's dead before touching wiring
Ladders: three points of contact, on firm ground, never on the top step
Gloves, safety glasses, and a dust mask when drilling or cutting
Never work on gas: in Dubai, gas work is for licensed, Civil Defence-approved specialists
slides.takeaway: A job done fast is no good if someone gets hurt. Isolate, test, protect.

slides.title: Tools and Home Systems
slides.body: A good technician carries a compact kit and knows where things are in a home: the DB, the main water valve, the water heater and the AC units.
bullets: Kit: multimeter or voltage tester, screwdrivers, adjustable spanner, pipe wrench, drill, sealant gun, torch, PTFE tape
UAE power: 230 V, 50 Hz, with three-pin Type G (BS 1363) sockets
Water heater thermostat at about 60°C: hot enough to stop Legionella bacteria
Know where the main water stopcock is before any plumbing job
slides.takeaway: Find the controls first: the DB, the stopcock and the heater. Then start work.

lab.title: Home Survey Lab
lab.brief: Survey a home: find the DB and label its circuits, find the main water valve, check the water heater setting and note the AC units.
lab.deliverable: A labelled home map with each control's location.
lab.proTip: A labelled DB saves you and the next technician time on every visit.

caseStudy.scenario: A tenant asks you to move a socket. The circuit is labelled 'sockets' but you haven't tested it. What now?

options.text: Switch off that breaker, test with a voltage tester that it's dead, then work.
options.explanation: Labels can be wrong: always test before touching.
Wrong labels are common and can kill.

quiz.question: What is the mains voltage in UAE homes?
quiz.explanation: UAE homes use 230 V at 50 Hz.

quiz.question: Who should work on gas installations?
quiz.explanation: Gas work is for approved specialists only.

weeks.title: Air Conditioning
weeks.objective: Understand split and central AC and do the maintenance that keeps it cold and efficient.

slides.title: How AC Works
slides.body: An air conditioner moves heat from inside to outside using refrigerant. The indoor unit (evaporator) absorbs heat from the room; the outdoor unit (condenser) releases it. In Dubai, AC runs most of the year, so poor maintenance shows up fast in bills and comfort.
bullets: Split units: an indoor and an outdoor unit joined by refrigerant pipes
Ducted and central AC: air through ducts; many towers use district cooling
Condensate drain: carries water away; if it blocks, water leaks indoors
Refrigerant work needs certified technicians
slides.takeaway: AC doesn't make cold: it moves heat out. Keep the airflow and the drain clear.

slides.title: Maintenance That Matters
slides.body: Most AC complaints are fixed with basic care: clean filters, clear drains and clean coils.
bullets: Clean or replace filters monthly in summer
Flush the condensate drain; clear algae with a mild cleaner
Keep outdoor units clear of dust and obstruction
Signs of a deeper problem: ice on pipes, warm air, loud noises: call a refrigeration technician
slides.example:
A 'not cooling' call, step by step:
1. Thermostat on Cool and set below room temperature? (Often the fix.)
2. Filter clogged with dust? Clean it.
3. Outdoor unit running, fan turning?
4. Ice on the pipes or warm air with everything clean: likely low refrigerant, so a specialist job.
slides.takeaway: A clean filter can cut cooling costs noticeably and stop most 'not cold' calls.

lab.title: AC Service Lab
lab.brief: Service a split unit: clean filters, check the drain, inspect the outdoor unit and record the air temperature at the vents before and after.
lab.deliverable: A service checklist with before and after vent temperatures.
lab.proTip: Show the customer the dirty filter: it builds trust and explains the value.

caseStudy.scenario: Water is dripping from an indoor AC unit onto the floor. What's most likely?

options.explanation: Refrigerant isn't water; leaks show as poor cooling, not drips.

options.text: The condensate drain is blocked: clear it.
options.explanation: Blocked drains are the usual cause of indoor drips.

options.text: The outdoor unit is too big.
options.explanation: Unit size doesn't cause indoor drips.

quiz.question: What does the outdoor (condenser) unit do?
options: Releases heat from the home outside
quiz.explanation: It rejects the heat taken out of the home.

quiz.question: How often should AC filters be cleaned in summer?
quiz.explanation: Monthly cleaning keeps airflow and efficiency up.

weeks.title: Plumbing and Electrical Basics
weeks.objective: Fix common plumbing faults, do simple electrical replacements safely and know your limits.

slides.title: Plumbing Fixes
slides.body: Most household plumbing jobs are leaks, blockages and running toilets. Isolate the water first and work clean.
bullets: Dripping tap: replace the washer or cartridge
Blocked sink: plunger first, then clean the P-trap; avoid harsh acids
Running toilet: adjust or replace the fill or flush valve
Hidden leak test: turn off all taps and watch the DEWA meter. If it moves, there's a leak
slides.takeaway: Isolate, fix, test, and leave it cleaner than you found it.

slides.title: Simple Electrical Jobs and Limits
slides.body: Replacing a light fitting, a socket faceplate or a plug is common handyman work when done safely. New circuits, DB changes and major rewiring need a licensed electrician and approvals.
bullets: Power off at the DB and test dead every time
Match the wires: live (brown), neutral (blue), earth (green and yellow)
RCDs (earth leakage breakers) trip at about 30 mA to protect people: if one keeps tripping, find the fault, don't bypass it
Know your limit: new circuits and DB work are for licensed electricians
slides.takeaway: Small jobs, done safely; big jobs, referred to licensed pros.

lab.title: Fault-Finding Lab
lab.brief: Diagnose and fix a dripping tap and a running toilet, then do a meter leak test for the whole home.
lab.deliverable: Photos, parts used, and the meter readings.
lab.proTip: Carry common washers, cartridges and flush valves: most jobs finish on the first visit.

caseStudy.scenario: A customer's RCD keeps tripping and they ask you to bypass it so the power stays on. What do you do?

options.explanation: An RCD protects people from electric shock. Bypassing it is dangerous and illegal.

options.text: Refuse to bypass it, unplug appliances one by one to find the fault, and call a licensed electrician if it's in the wiring.
options.explanation: Find the faulty appliance or circuit and keep the protection working.

options.text: Swap it for a bigger breaker.
options.explanation: That removes protection and creates a fire risk.

quiz.question: Earth wire colour in UAE wiring?
Water meter moves with all taps off. This means:
quiz.explanation: Movement with nothing on means water is escaping somewhere.

weeks.title: Quoting and Running Jobs
weeks.objective: Price work fairly, communicate like a professional and build repeat customers.

slides.title: Quoting a Job
slides.body: Clear, written quotes prevent arguments. Break them into labour, materials and call-out, add your margin, and say what's included.
bullets: Labour: hours × your hourly rate
Materials: cost plus a markup for sourcing
Call-out or minimum charge
VAT at 5% if you're VAT-registered
slides.example:
Replacing a kitchen mixer tap:
• Labour: 1.5 hours × AED 120 = AED 180
• Tap supplied: AED 350 cost + 15% = AED 402.50
• Call-out: AED 50
Total: AED 632.50, plus 5% VAT if registered = AED 664.13
slides.takeaway: A clear quote is half the job: it sets expectations and protects you both.

slides.title: Customer Service and Repeat Work
slides.body: Customers remember punctuality, tidiness and honesty more than anything. Annual maintenance contracts (AMCs) for AC and general upkeep turn one-off jobs into steady income.
bullets: Arrive on time, or call ahead if you're late
Protect floors, clean up, and explain what you did
Photos before and after build trust
Offer an AMC: AC servicing every 3 to 4 months plus priority call-outs
slides.takeaway: Honest, tidy and on time: that's how one job becomes ten.

lab.title: Quote and AMC Lab
lab.brief: Write quotes for three common jobs and design an annual maintenance contract for a 2-bedroom apartment.
lab.deliverable: Three itemised quotes and a one-page AMC offer with price.
lab.proTip: Price the AMC so it's cheaper than ad-hoc calls for the customer but steady income for you.

caseStudy.scenario: Halfway through a job you find a bigger problem that will double the cost. What do you do?

options.text: Fix it and add it to the bill.
Stop, show the customer, explain options and costs, and get their OK before continuing.
options.explanation: Customers decide on extra cost. Transparency keeps trust.

quiz.question: What is an AMC?
quiz.explanation: An annual maintenance contract brings repeat work.
